title: micro-assembly-kits-notebook
content:
Quick notes / messy sketch for a tiny product idea: Micro Assembly Kits (MAKs) — small, composable response templates + tooling to speed up building features that assemble LLM output, external data, and tool calls.

Context / why:
- We keep building one-off features where engineering wires prompts + a couple of tool calls + template glue. Lots of duplication and slow iteration.
- For hosted customers we want a low-friction way to ship composed responses (e.g., conversational summaries with citations, multi-step data fetch + synthesis, formatted code responses) without full engineering cycle every time.
- Goal: give product teams a lightweight building block (kit) that is reusable, versioned, and safe-by-default.

High-level idea:
- MAK = small manifest + template + optional tool bindings + test prompt set.
- Manifest declares inputs, permission surface (e.g., needs DB read, needs API X), and preferred model/quantization profile.
- Runtime executes: 1) fetch external inputs via bound tool hooks (or static sample), 2) run one or more LLM calls (with KV-cache/prefix behavior), 3) apply local post-processing template (mustache-ish) -> output.
- Kits are shareable across projects, can be pinned to model versions, and have per-kit telemetry (tokens, latency, error).

User personas / user stories (rough):
- PM (Sara): "I want to prototype a help center answer that pulls latest KB paragraph and synthesizes a short answer with steps." -> Picks KB-summary kit, binds KB tool, supplies tone param, prototypes in console.
- Platform eng (Dev): "I need to ship a ticket generator that scrubs sensitive fields and includes stack traces." -> Uses code-safe kit with redaction tool, pins to dedicated infra.
- Solutions eng (Alex): "I want a canned onboarding response that can also call billing API for account age." -> Uses kit with optional callouts, tests with sample data.

Core components to design:
- Kit manifest schema (YAML/JSON): inputs, outputs, tool bindings, model hints, cache hints, risk score, allowed tokens budget.
- UI: kit gallery in Console (filter by category, risk level, latency profile). Quick test harness: fill inputs -> run -> inspect tool calls and LLM trace.
- Runtime: sandboxed tool adapter layer + templating engine + LLM call pipeline supporting multi-shot and KV-cache reuse.
- CI: per-kit test suite (prompt set + expected assertions) and regression alerts in Optimize.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create / save a kit with manifest + template in Console.
- Bind a mock tool (simple HTTP data source) and run a kit from Console with sample inputs.
- Runtime logs show: tool calls, token usage, latency, and model response.
- Kit can be pinned to a model version (hosted), and we can fallback to a compatible variant.

Non-goals (initial):
- Not building a full visual flow editor yet.
- Not supporting complex stateful multi-turn orchestration (beyond simple sequential steps) in MVP.

Technical notes / constraints:
- KV cache reuse: try to reuse per-kit prefix for repeated runs in a session to reduce cost. Kits that only fill templates should be eligible for aggressive caching.
- Batching: long-running kits might be queued into batch windows; need QoS tag in manifest.
- Security: manifest declares required scopes; runtime enforces policies (no direct DB writes without whitelist). Redaction hooks mandatory for any kit that accepts user-uploaded text.
- Telemetry: per-kit metrics (median p50/p99 latency, tokens per call, external tool error rate). Integrate with Console rollouts.

UX sketches / flow (notes-to-self):
- Console -> "Create kit" -> small form (name, category, risk) -> paste template + manifest -> Save.
- Test tab: sample inputs (key/val), run -> trace viewer (tool calls timeline on left, LLM tokens/stream preview on right, template output below).
- Quick-publish: make kit private, or share with workspace, or publish to org kit gallery.

Example manifest (informal):
- id: billing-quick-fix-v1
- inputs: ["account_id","error_log"]
- tools: [{name:billing-api, scope:read, url:aws:lambda:billing:...}]
- model_hints: {preferred: redwood-1-medium, fallback: redwood-1-small}
- cache: {mode:prefix, ttl:3600}
- safety: {redaction: true, max_response_tokens: 300}

Example template (pseudo):
- prompt: |
  You are a concise assistant. Using data from {{billing_api.latest_invoice}} and the account age for {{account_id}}, create a 3-bullet resolution plan. Keep it neutral tone.
  ---
  Output:

Open questions / risks (TODO):
- Ownership model: who vets kits for org-wide gallery (solutions eng? security?)
- Runtime cost model: do we charge per-kit or instrument via existing per-token usage? (probably existing usage)
- Model compatibility: manifest hints vs enforced pinned version; lazy fallback vs strict pinning.
- Can kits call customer-owned private tools in Private deployments? need policy mapping.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: internal-only proto (console + mock tools) + tiny kit gallery. (1 sprint)
- Phase 1: customer beta with 3 partner teams + telemetry + test harness (3 sprints)
- Phase 2: gallery + sharing + basic approval workflow (2 sprints)

Metrics to track (early):
- #kits created per org, conversion to published kit, average tokens/run, latency distribution, number of kit-based endpoints in prod.

Next immediate TODOs (me):
- Wire up a tiny manifest schema draft and push to GH (INF-4823 branch).
- Mock Console sketch (Priya / Mika for UX feedback) — schedule 30m sync.
- Add 5 example kits: KB-summary, billing-fix, code-format, onboarding-short, redaction-demo.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could we provide 'kit adapters' for common SaaS (Zendesk, Notion, Stripe) so product teams just pick a connector? (saves wiring)
- Kit-level QA: small eval harness that runs a few golden prompts and checks for hallucination/citation quality. Hook into Optimize to send alerts when a kit's quality regresses.
- Consider a tiny DSL for post-processing (safe sanitize, truncate, enforce JSON schema).
- UX: make "test with sample data" frictionless (drag-and-drop sample payloads).

References / related tickets: INF-4823 (manifest sketch), PR #2101 (runtime adapter spike), slack thread #product-microkits-thread (notes from Jan 10 brainstorm).

Random: If this works, could save ~2-3 weeks per small feature for partner teams. That latency/cost improvement messaging might be a good GTM angle (developer time saved + predictable token cost).

-- end of notebook dump --
